testEffect: The test both writes to and reads from the module-level `history` array (`record(...)` then `history().length`), so its own act and its own assertion share one mutable module-level array instead of the test owning independent state.
productionEffect: Running this exact test body twice in a row within the same process, sharing one loaded `audit-log` module without resetting it between runs (as the real 11-test suite does), is expected to keep passing on the second run even if `record` is corrupted into a no-op on that run alone — the first run's own call already left `history()` non-empty. Only a single execution against a freshly loaded module can tell a working `record` from a broken one; repeated execution that shares module state, exactly as this suite does, cannot re-verify it after the first pass.
